beats.text: Most apologies miss the most important part!
Researchers tested six parts of an apology with over seven hundred people.
Number one: own it. Say: this was my fault!
Number two: offer to fix it. And the least useful part?
So: own it. Fix it. Don't beg!

ask: SAVE THIS FOR YOUR NEXT SORRY.
sources: Lewicki, Polin & Lount (2016), An exploration of the structure of effective apologies, Negotiation and Conflict Management Research 9(2) – 333 adults online + 422 students: acknowledgment of responsibility most important, then offer of repair; request for forgiveness least important.
